results.title: Recap: the OVHcloud Blog from August 2026 | Highlights
results.author: OVHcloud Team
highlights:
#### Public Cloud: the end of the all-in-one plan

As of October 1, local storage and the public IPv4 address will move out of instance prices and onto their own lines, while compute prices will stay put. The article explains the two reasons behind the new à la carte model, namely: to stay comparable with market practices, and to hold the line on compute because memory costs six times more than it did a year ago. Discover the new model.

#### Public Cloud pricing: the details, effective October 1

To break it all down: for an identical configuration, increases can range from 1.4% to 21.9% across B3, C3, and R3 instances, with a reference-by-reference table and four architecture examples to size up your own case. Savings Plans get simpler too — two terms, 12 months (-15%) and 36 months (-30%), starting September 1. Run the numbers for your instances.

#### Dedicated servers: what changes in the second half of 2026

There will be no across-the-board increase here. Prices are adjusted reference by reference on the Advance, Game, Scale, and High Grade ranges (Gen 2024 and 2026), while Kimsufi, So you Start, Rise, and earlier generations stay the same. Existing customers get the softer landing: their renewal increase is three to six times smaller than for a new order, and a prepaid subscription will lock in today's price. Check what changes for your servers.

results.title: OVHcloud October 2026 Price Change: Disk and IPv4 Split Out
results.author: StackValue Editorial
highlights:
What changes in OVHcloud Public Cloud pricing on 1 October 2026?

From 1 October 2026 OVHcloud bills local NVMe storage and the public IPv4 address separately on B3, C3 and R3 instances: storage at €0.0001458 per GB per hour, about €0.11 per GB a month, and IPv4 at €0.0027 per hour, about €1.97 a month. The hourly instance price does not change. For an identical configuration the bill rises 1.4% to 21.9%: b3-8 €37 to €45, c3-4 €33 to €41, r3-16 €48 to €56 a month. Older generations (B2, C2, R2) keep storage included.

...

Updated 8 September 2026. Our daily price watch caught the OVHcloud price list adding the same 1 October notice to five more ranges: Storage Optimized, Discovery, GPU, Metal and Gateway all lose the included IPv4 address on that date. Only b3, c3 and r3 lose the local disk as well. The table below now covers all eight. Updated 7 September 2026. The sentence on stated causes in the ledger section now quotes each vendor’s own wording; the earlier version said all four cited memory and storage costs, which is true of OVHcloud and Scaleway only. Every entry below is also a row in our 2026 infrastructure price change ledger.

KEY FINDING. From 1 October 2026, OVHcloud’s Generation 3 Public Cloud instances (B3, C3, R3) stop including local storage and a public IPv4 address. Both become separate lines: local NVMe at €0.0001458 per GB per hour, about €0.11 per GB a month, and IPv4 at €0.0027 per hour, about €1.97 a month. The hourly instance price does not move. For an identical configuration OVHcloud’s own table shows the bill rising 1.4% to 21.9%, and the smallest sizes take the biggest hit: b3-8 €37 to €45, c3-4 €33 to €41, r3-16 €48 to €56 a month. Two levers cut most of it: release IPv4 addresses that instances do not need, and use the flex variants, whose local disk is fixed at 50 GB. A b3-64 rises 14.9% as a standard instance and 2.3% as a flex.

...

Two posts by Octave Klaba, both dated 25 August 2026, carry the change. The model post: “these two resources will become separate billable lines. The price of the virtual machine, or the compute, will not change.” The detail post gives the range: “the increase in price ranges from 1.4% to 21.9%, dependent on size.” The stated reason is component cost: “Buying memory costs us six times more today than it did a year ago, and storage is following the same trajectory.” The stated design choice is to make the increase actionable rather than flat: “an IP address that serves no purpose can be released, or an oversized volume can be reduced.”

results.title: OVHcloud GPU Alternative (2026): GPU Prices vs PowerGPU
highlights:
OVHcloud is a European infrastructure provider built around data sovereignty: self-service Public Cloud GPU instances (H100, A100, L40S, L4) billed hourly, plus dedicated Scale and HGR-AI bare-metal GPU servers sold by quote outside the self-service catalog. The current H100/A100/L40S/L4 flavors are concentrated in a single region, Gravelines (GRA11), while OVHcloud's non-GPU Public Cloud spans dozens of datacenters across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific. Billing is hourly, payment is by card or SEPA, and most European and North American datacenters include unlimited outbound bandwidth.

results.title: OVHcloud Price Increase 2026: Both Waves, in Full
results.author: Capital, Compute
highlights:
- → Two waves. Announced 5 March 2026 (effective April) covering Public Cloud, Bare Metal and VPS, and announced 17 August 2026 covering dedicated servers, with dates of 1 July for options, 11 August for new configurations and 1 October for existing customers at renewal.
- → The 9 to 11 percent average from the March announcement is real but unrepresentative: the VPS 2026 range in the same announcement moved about 44 to 48 percent, with VPS-1 going from 4.49 to 6.49 euros a month.
- → The August wave is graded by hardware generation. Advance Gen 2024 rose 16 to 36 percent while Advance Gen 2026 rose 25 to 74 percent, because the newer generation carries DDR5.
- → Memory sold as an option rose 68 to 652 percent on new orders, against 8 to 166 percent for storage. Whole servers rose far less, because memory is only part of a server price.
- → Existing customers are reached from 1 October 2026 at renewal, with RAM upgrades up 20 percent on Gen 2024 and 40 percent on Gen 2026. Kimsufi, So you Start and Rise were left alone.

...

OVHcloud announced on 5 March 2026 that it was adjusting prices across Public Cloud, Bare Metal and VPS, effective in April. It attributed this to a global memory market that had been disrupted since autumn 2025 by an industrial shift toward GPUs, which reduced stock and extended lead times.

...

The second announcement, published 17 August, is the one that produced the up-to-87-percent headlines. It covers dedicated servers and splits into three dates: memory and storage option pricing from 1 July 2026, new server configuration pricing from 11 August, and existing customers at renewal from 1 October.

...

For most existing OVHcloud customers the answer is 1 October 2026, at renewal. That is the date the second wave applies to existing contracts, and it is when the majority of people will actually notice, months after the headlines.

# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

...

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

...

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

...

results.title: Nebius raises hourly GPU rates up to 21% from 1st October · The Inference
results.author: Richard Tang
highlights:
Nvidia H100 accelerators, the workhorse of neocloud rate cards. From 1 October an on-demand hour on one at Nebius costs $4.50, up from $3.85.
